I independently compared the complete source def:deletion-halves (reference/SM/sm-1-polygons.tex, lines 1227–1240) with SM.deletion_halves_definition, the printed DeletionHalvesDefinitionData/DeletionData/HalvesData structures, the actual child definitions and their supporting proof bodies. Every source definition and directed-edge convention is covered.

Deletion domain and meaning. The first branch quantifies every natural child size k≥3 and every labelled parent tuple of size k+1, hence exactly every source parent size n≥4. The NeZero k witness is redundant under k≥3. No flat-wall, Generic, regularity, embedding or geometric-position hypothesis is imposed on this definition. deleteVertex is the actual parent tuple composed with deletionIndex. That index map is proved injective, omits the marked label and exhausts every other parent label. It starts at the old successor j+1, ends at j−1, and advances by the parent successor except at the child's closing step. Thus it retains exactly the induced cyclic order, with a concrete representative cut. Every ordinary directed edge is the corresponding actual parent edge; the closing edge is the actual vector P_(j+1)−P_(j−1). These are statements about the constructed tuple, rather than freely supplied data satisfying a deletion-like interface.

Halves domain and exact ranges. The second branch quantifies the actual centre of every simple vertex-edge WallGerm under the printed VertexEdgeAt predicate. The four-label separation, sole zero triple, absence of remote concurrence, interior contact and actual chi sign change are the inherited source conditions, not substitutes for them. The constructed halves only need the separation and interior-contact facts for this definition. Put d=(a−M).val. The first half has d+1 labels and sends i to M+i.val, so its sequence is M,M+1,...,a. The second has n−d labels, sends zero to M and every other i to a+i.val, giving M,a+1,...,M−1. Its exact range is proved by identifying it with the rotation i↦i−1 of the consecutive range beginning at a+1; it is not an arbitrary list or a reversed traversal. Both actual label maps are proved injective, and the range, first/last, successor and endpoint formulas cover all labels and modular wraparound. The inherited separation proof yields 2≤d≤n−3, so both sizes are at least three; their inclusive bounds are explicitly proved in the companion full children lemma. Under the source's count-only relabelling M=1,a=k, d=k−1, so the sizes become k and n−k+1 exactly as printed.

Directed ordinary and cut edges. The first half follows E_M,...,E_(a−1) and closes from P_a to P_M. The second opens from P_M to P_(a+1), follows the indicated consecutive parent edges, and its last ordinary edge is E_(M−1), closing back at P_M. For the actual contact P_M=P_a+r·edge(P,a), the definition data supply one real witness 0<r<1. The closing vector of the first half is r·edge(P,a), and the opening vector of the second is (1−r)·edge(P,a), both positive multiples in the source orientation. The exact affine point formulas hold for every real child parameter t: the parent parameters are r*t and r+(1−r)*t. The explicit closed-segment inclusion proofs use 0≤t≤1 and retain both endpoints; the strict interior inclusion proofs use 0<t<1 and place each cut interior strictly inside the parent E_a. The remaining edge points are unchanged parent edge points. Thus the source subsegment assertions concern the finite segments, not merely their supporting lines.

Cyclic representative fidelity. The source permits labelled formalization with proved cyclic equivariance. Under shift r, parent labels become j−r or M−r,a−r. Deletion of the shifted marked tuple is proved equal to the same canonically cut child. Both halves are likewise coordinatewise unchanged after transporting the proved equal natural sizes. Their HEq statements only express that size transport; after rewriting the unchanged distance, the proofs are ordinary pointwise equalities. They do not identify an unrelated polygon, reverse orientation or insert an assumed child relabelling. These exact marked relabelling laws justify the labelled representatives of the source polygon constructions.

Printed object (reference/SM/sm-1-polygons.tex:1254-1267, SM15 excerpt byte-identical to SM12; not in CHANGES_SINCE_20260909.md section 1): (1) for n>=4 and j in Z/n, P\j is the (n-1)-tuple omitting mu_j with the induced cyclic order; (2) at a simple vertex-edge wall at (M;a), b=a+1, the halves at the centre P(0) are lambda_1=(mu_M,...,mu_a) and lambda_2=(mu_M,mu_b,...,mu_{M-1}), where lambda_1 follows E_M..E_{a-1} and closes with [mu_a,mu_M] subset E_a, and lambda_2 opens with [mu_M,mu_b] subset E_a, follows E_b..E_{M-2}, closes with E_{M-1}.

Lean (work/lean/SM/DeletionHalvesDefinition.lean:99-107): DeletionHalvesDefinitionData is the conjunction of (i) for all k>=3, all P : LabelledTuple (k+1), all j : ZMod (k+1), DeletionData P j, i.e. parent size k+1>=4 exactly as printed; and (ii) for all k>=3, all g : WallGerm k and M a with g.VertexEdgeAt M a, HalvesData g.center M a. VertexEdgeAt (NamedWallPredicates.lean:19-22) is clause (V) of def:walls verbatim: M not in {a-1,a,a+1,a+2}, pointZeros={ {a,a+1,M} }, concurrences=empty, center M in relint E_a(center), and sign change of chi_{a,a+1,M}; g.center = g.curve 0 (WallGerm.lean:30), so 'all vertices at t=0' is met.

Definitions denote the printed objects. deleteVertex P j i = P (deletionIndex j i) with deletionIndex j i = (i.val : ZMod (n+1)) + (j+1) (DeletedTuple.lean:13, DeletionIndices.lean:11): the representative (mu_{j+1}, mu_{j+2}, ..., mu_{j-1}), i.e. omit mu_j and keep the induced cyclic order; DeletionData records injectivity, omission of j, exhaustion of every other label, first/last labels j+1 and j-1, successor law, inherited edges, fused closing edge mu_{j+1}-mu_{j-1}, and shift-equivariance. firstHalfSize=(a-M).val+1, secondHalfSize=n-(a-M).val (ContactHalfSizes.lean:10-14); firstHalf P M a i = P (M + i.val) gives (mu_M,...,mu_a); secondHalf P M a i = P (if i=0 then M else a+i.val) gives (mu_M, mu_{a+1}, ..., mu_{M-1}) since a+(n-(a-M).val-1) = M-1 (ContactHalfTuples.lean:11-15, ContactHalfIndices.lean:18-25, CyclicRangeIndices.lean:11). HalvesData fields first_edges/second_edges give edges E_M..E_{a-1} and E_b..E_{M-1} respectively; first_/second_segment_inclusions at i=-1 resp. i=0 give the closing segment [mu_a,mu_M] subset E_a and opening segment [mu_M,mu_b] subset E_a (firstHalfIndex M a (-1) = a, secondHalfEdgeIndex M a 0 = a); cut_segments exhibits the contact parameter 0<r<1 with closing vector r*edge_a and opening vector (1-r)*edge_a and exact reparametrisations; first_range/second_range pin the vertex sets to {M..a} and {b..M}. Halves are given as labelled representatives with mu_M first and shift-equivariance (HEq across the propositionally equal sizes) recorded, which the formalization remark after def:polygon (sm-1-polygons.tex:53-61) expressly permits. Hypotheses 3<=k and NeZero k are implied by the printed context (a vertex-edge wall forces n>=5; deletion needs n>=4) so nothing is over-restricted, and VertexEdgeAt is satisfiable so nothing is vacuous. Module compiles (olean present) and the file hashes match the accepted review. The existing review (work/reviews/def-deletion-halves.json) reaches the same verdict; I agree with it.
stronger_than_source: DeletionData records several immediate consequences the printed definition leaves implicit (fused closing edge P(j+1)-P(j-1), explicit first/last labels, injectivity and exhaustion of the label map) and exact shift-equivariance deleteVertex (shift r P) (j-r) = deleteVertex P j as a representative-level equality.

HalvesData records the explicit contact parameter r with closing/opening edge vectors r*edge_a and (1-r)*edge_a, edge-point reparametrisations, and interior-segment inclusions, beyond the printed 'subset E_a'; all are true consequences of the printed object, not extra hypotheses.

The characterisation is stated for every wall germ satisfying VertexEdgeAt; the underlying definitions firstHalf/secondHalf/deleteVertex are total functions on arbitrary tuples (harmless: the printed content is asserted exactly in the printed context).
